source_refs.note: Topic 8.5, printed page 171 (Figure 8.2, carried by the dynamic equilibrium original), with Quick Check 8.3 (c) as the self-check.

items: The state of equilibrium applies only to reversible reactions.
Equilibrium can be established only if the reaction vessel is closed, so that no part of the reactants or products escapes.

blocks.text: For CaCO3(s) giving CaO(s) + CO2(g), equilibrium is established in a closed system, where the carbon dioxide stays in contact with the solids, but not in an open system, where the gas escapes and cannot recombine.

blocks.prompt: In a soda-water bottle gaseous CO2 is in equilibrium with dissolved CO2, CO2(g) + H2O(l) giving HCO3-(aq) + H+(aq). Why does this equilibrium require the cap to be closed, and which way does it shift when the cap is removed?
blocks.explanation: With the cap on, the CO2 that escapes from the solution stays in the bottle and dissolves again at the same rate, so the system is closed and equilibrium holds. Removing the cap lets the gas escape; the reverse reaction then has nothing to recombine, so the equilibrium shifts to the left, dissolved CO2 keeps leaving as bubbles, and the drink goes flat.

items: Equilibrium needs a reversible reaction and a closed vessel; CaCO3 and CO2 reach equilibrium only when the gas cannot escape.
